A three-panel diagram showing the morphology of weeds. Left panel: A grass weed showing a round hollow stem with swollen nodes, long narrow leaves with parallel veins, and fibrous roots. Middle panel: A sedge showing a solid triangular cross-section stem without nodes, and grass-like leaves. Right panel: A broadleaf weed showing a solid branching stem, wide leaves with net-veins, and a distinct thick taproot.

An illustration showing four methods of weed seed dispersal. Top left (Wind): a fluffy Tridax seed with a hair-like parachute being blown by wind lines. Top right (Animal): a spiky Boerhavia seed stuck to the fabric of a farmer's trousers. Bottom left (Water): a smooth seed floating on a cross-section of a water stream. Bottom right (Explosive): a dry leguminous weed pod twisting and bursting open, flinging small round seeds outward.
